source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Increase the number of daily dosing times when possible because a more complex schedule makes each dose more noticeable and therefore improves adherence.","B":"Focus on medication education without asking about cost, side effects, or confusion because those barriers are separate from adherence counseling.","C":"Simplify the regimen when possible, link doses to daily routines, and use pill organizers or electronic reminders tailored to the client's barriers.","D":"Use counseling without reminder tools because pill organizers, routines, and electronic prompts add complexity without improving day-to-day adherence."}}
source_row.rationale: Adherence improves when regimens and reminders are made easier and barriers are addressed. Option C is correct because AHRQ recommends simplifying dosing when possible, linking doses to routines, and using pill organizers or electronic reminders. Option A increases complexity. Option B ignores common adherence barriers. Option D rejects practical reminder strategies that AHRQ recommends.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 16 — Help Patients Take Medicine Correctly: identify adherence barriers; simplify medication schedules when possible; link doses with daily routines; use pill organizers, charts, family supports, alarms or electronic reminders as appropriate to the individual's barriers. AHRQ Tool 16 last reviewed 2024-04 and remains current on the federal AHRQ site; live source rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive care, immunization, pregnancy health promotion, adherence support and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality — Help Patients Take Medicine Correctly: Tool 16
source_row.stem: A client frequently misses doses because the medication schedule is complex and easy to forget. Which intervention best supports adherence?
